title: Optogenetic axon guidance in embryonic zebrafish
protocol: Prepare 1% agarose mounting solution.
Weigh out the appropriate amount of agarose (0.05 g agarose/5 mL E3 with 0.0168% tricaine).
Add agarose to E3 with 0.0168% tricaine and stir to form a homogenous suspension.
Microwave suspension until completely dissolved, around 10 s at high power.
Place dissolved agarose solution in a pre-equilibrated water bath at 42°C to cool for about 30 min.
Ensure zebrafish are the appropriate age for stimulation experiments.
Dissect the chorion away from the zebrafish embryos with fine forceps.
Dissect embryos using fine forceps by pinching the chorion with one pair of forceps.
Use a second pair of forceps to peel away the chorion.
Transfer embryos to 0.0168% tricaine in E3 solution for 5 minutes.
Ensure embryos are adequately anesthetized by lightly brushing their tails with a gel-loading pipette tip.
Remove the anesthetic solution from the microcentrifuge tube, taking care not to damage or remove the embryos.
Add agarose mounting solution pre-cooled to 42°C to the embryos in the tube.
Transfer zebrafish embryos to glass bottom dishes for positioning.
Add the minimum volume of agarose necessary to cover the surface of the glass for zebrafish mounting.
Position embryos on their side such that the longitudinal axis is parallel to the bottom of the dish with an eye facing up.
Monitor embryo position continuously as the agarose solidifies and adjust as needed.
Slowly add 1 ml of E3 solution with tricaine anesthetic to the glass bottom dish to keep the agarose hydrated after it solidifies for 15 min.
Wrap the glass bottom dish with mounted zebrafish in tinfoil to avoid ambient light exposure.
Use the Zeiss LSM 880 Microscope for optogenetic axon guidance experiments.
Ensure the microscope is equipped with a GaAsP or Airyscan high-sensitivity detector.
Reduce ambient light by turning off room lights and covering the microscope with a blackout curtain.
Turn computer screens away from the microscope to minimize background illumination.
Cover microscope indicator lights beneath the blackout curtain with tape.
Measure and minimize baseline activation of PA-Rac1 as described in Step 34.
Power on the laser, microscope, and computer.
Launch the microscope control software (Zen Black).
Preheat the incubation chamber and stage incubator to 28.5°C if equipped.
Move a tinfoil-wrapped glass-bottom dish under the blackout curtain.
Unwrap the tinfoil and position the dish on the microscope stage.
Set up the imaging laser, light path, filters, and standard detector with Smart Setup.
Select mCherry from the dropdown menu under “Dye” in the top left panel.
False color the greyscale image by selecting a color under the “Color” dropdown menu.
Choose the “Fastest” imaging strategy.
Click “Apply” to enable the appropriate excitation laser and emission filters.
Enable the T-PMT in the “Imaging Setup” panel to enable a brightfield channel from transmitted fluorescent light.
Check the line with the standard “Ch1” detector and set the dye to “mCherry”.
Set the emission spectrum range to 578–697nm for mCherry.
Ensure that the appropriate filters are in place for the selected detectors and dyes.
Enable any high-sensitivity detectors such as GaAsP or Airyscan, if required.
Input DIC optics parameters from the microscope control touch screen into the Zen software under the “Locate” tab.
Click the checkbox next to “GaAsP2” in the “Imaging Setup” panel to enable if using a GaAsP detector.
Ensure the appropriate bandpass filter for the mCherry emission spectrum (575–610nm) is used with the GaAsP detector.
In the “Imaging Setup” panel, click the checkbox next to the “ChA” detector if using an Airyscan detector.
Disable the standard “Ch1” detector when enabling the “ChA” detector in the imaging setup panel.
Ensure the appropriate filter set allowing light from the mCherry emission spectrum (575–610nm) is upstream of the “ChA” detector.
Select “SR” (super resolution) as the Airyscan Mode in the “Channels” panel.
Ensure the Airyscan detector is properly aligned for imaging.
Click “Continuous” to generate a live image.
Focus on a small fluorescent feature in the mCherry channel during alignment.
Open the “Airyscan” panel under the “Maintain tab” and adjust X and Y positions until central hexagons are brightest.
Adjust position settings until the “Quality and Status” indicator reads “Good (Waiting)”.
Click “Store Current Pos” to save this position.
Set up differential interference contrast (DIC) optics.
Determine the DIC condenser and numerical aperture (NA) for imaging.
Input parameters in Zen software matching those of the objective.
Keep laser power as low as possible to prevent photobleaching and toxicity.
Locate mounted zebrafish embryos using a low magnification objective.
Adjust focus, laser power, and master gain until fish and neurons appear clearly.
Screen mounted zebrafish for appropriately positioned healthy fish at the correct developmental timepoint.
Ensure robust mCherry-PA-Rac1 expression in the CaP spinal motor neurons.
Adjust digital zoom to quickly locate and screen zebrafish.
Identify a zebrafish as an appropriate candidate for optogenetic stimulation.
Select a CaP spinal motor neuron to target for optogenetic axon guidance.
Aim for central CaP axons above the end of the yolk sac extension.
Use neighboring neurons as internal controls for optogenetic stimulation.
Switch to a higher-power objective (Plan-Apochromat 20x/0.8 M27).
Bring the target neuron into focus.
Click the “Snap” button to generate a single image using the current settings.
Adjust the frame size until snapshots of the target neurons are of sufficient quality.
Adjust the scan speed until snapshots of the target neurons are of sufficient quality.
Adjust pixel averaging until snapshots of the target neurons are of sufficient quality.
Adjust digital zoom until snapshots of the target neurons are of sufficient quality.
Set the laser power at the lowest level possible (<2%) that still produces a clear image to prevent photobleaching.
Adjust the master gain of the detector until snapshots of the target neurons are of sufficient quality.
Enable Z-stack imaging by clicking the “Z-Stack” checkbox.
Set the first image plane by focusing the microscope at the top of the desired Z-stack and click the corresponding button.
Set the last image plane by focusing the microscope at the bottom of the desired Z-stack and click the corresponding button.
Press the "Optimal" button to automatically calculate the appropriate slice number and thickness based on the current parameters.
Click “Start Experiment” to acquire high-quality Z-stack images.
Perform post-imaging deconvolution if using the Airyscan detector.
Go to the “Processing” tab and click “Airyscan Processing.”
Select the appropriate image for deconvolution.
Ensure 3D deconvolution is selected and click “Apply.”
Adjust the strength of the Wiener filter to optimize deconvolution.
Save current imaging settings to a profile.
Restore previous imaging settings by clicking the “Reuse” button in the “Dimensions” panel.
Deliver light stimulation every 1–3 seconds during optogenetic axon guidance experiments.
Acquire an image between each light stimulus to monitor axon growth.
Repeat stimulation and imaging cycles until the axon grows sufficiently.
Acquire high-quality 3D Z-stack images in the mCherry channel before and after optogenetic stimulation experiment.
Acquire 2D single plane images in the mCherry channel during axon guidance experiment over a period of 1-7 seconds using the 561nm laser.
Immediately following image acquisition, photoactivate PA-Rac1 for 2 ms using the 458 nm laser within a region of interest 3-30 μm.
Repeat imaging-stimulation cycle to induce axonal outgrowth into the region of interest.
Focus on the leading edge of the growth cone of the neuron targeted for optogenetic axon guidance.
Use a higher-power objective (Plan-Apochromat 20x/0.8 NA M27) for continued use.
Acquire a test image by clicking the “Snap” button.
Adjust the parameters until satisfactory images are acquired, ensuring that the image duration is less than 3 seconds and laser power is less than 2%.
Enable time-lapse imaging by checking the “Time Series” box and unchecking the “Z-Stack” box.
Enter the maximal number of cycles (100,000) with an interval of 0 milliseconds between imaging cycles.
Manually stop the time series acquisition when the axon has grown sufficiently to require an update to the region of illumination.
Redraw the region of illumination and restart time-lapse imaging as needed.
Enable focal optogenetic stimulation by checking “Bleaching” and “Regions”.
Illuminate with laser light at a wavelength of 458 nm and power of 5% in a user-drawn region of interest (ROI).
Acquire an image by clicking the “Snap” button.
Draw a 3-30 μm diameter circular ROI using the circle icon at the leading edge of the growth cone facing the desired direction of growth.
Measure the amount of light delivered during optogenetic stimulation with an optical power meter (ThorLabs PM100D).
Remove the sample dish with the mounted zebrafish embryo from the stage.
Take a baseline optical power reading while the microscope is turned on, but not active to measure background illumination.
Minimize background illumination by turning off or blocking lights with tape or blackout curtains.
Increase the iterations of bleaching to the maximum value.
Click "Start Experiment" to initiate the imaging experiment.
Measure the laser power during the stimulation period.
Adjust laser power such that the power meter reads between 300–650 nW total power in a 3–10 um diameter circular region of interest (21–32 mW/mm²).
Replace the sample dish and refocus on the growth cone of the target axon.
Repeat Step to ensure the ROI is drawn appropriately on the growth cone.
Reduce the bleaching iterations to the specified value.
Start time-lapse imaging and optogenetic axon guidance by clicking the “Start Experiment” button.
Monitor axonal growth, adjusting the focus as needed, until the growth cone fully occupies the ROI.
Click "Finish current step" to manually terminate the imaging experiment when necessary.
Refocus on the growth cone as necessary.
Delete the previous ROI and draw an updated ROI as in Step 33.
Resume time lapse imaging and optogenetic stimulation with the new ROI by pressing the “Start Experiment” button.
Repeat step until axon grows to the desired location.
Acquire a high-quality Z-stack by repeating Steps 21-26 to capture detailed axonal morphology after axonal guidance.
Use previously saved settings to expedite the imaging setup.
Remove zebrafish from agarose using a small scalpel carefully dissecting away embedding media.
Transfer fish to 28.5°C E3 culture media without Tricaine anesthetic for further development or analysis.
Grow zebrafish for 1.5 hours following optogenetic axon guidance in E3 culture media without tricaine anesthetic at 28.5°C.
Fix embryos in fixing solution overnight (12-16 h) at 4°C.
Wash embryos three times for five minutes in washing solution (PBT).
Separate the zebrafish head from the tail using a miniature scalpel.
Incubate tails for 45 min in 1 mg/mL collagenase in PBS.
Wash tails three times in washing solution for five minutes.
Incubate tails in blocking solution for several hours.
Incubate with mouse anti-synaptic vesicle 2 (1:100) and rabbit anti-RFP (1:500) primary antibodies in blocking solution overnight (12-16 hr) at 4°C.
Wash embryo tails 5 times with PBT.
Incubate overnight at 4°C with AlexaFluor 488 conjugated goat anti-mouse (1:750) and AlexaFluor 546 conjugated goat anti-rabbit (1:750) secondary antibodies in blocking solution.
Add AlexFluor 647-conjugated α-bungarotoxin (1:500) during the last 45 minutes of incubation with secondary antibodies.
Wash embryo tails three times for five minutes each in washing solution.
Mount embryo tails in 1% low melting point agarose in PBS for confocal imaging.
Image samples.
